_comment: RTDB rules for the territory_views counter. MERGE this into the project's
existing rules alongside daily_scans — do not paste it over them.
The page writes anonymously, so without a rule anyone could set a counter
to any number. These counts are meant to steer how the system evolves, so
a poisoned counter is not a vanity problem — it is someone steering the
mood engine. The write rule allows ONLY +1 from the current value, so a
counter cannot be set to an arbitrary number, cannot be lowered, and
WHAT IT DOES NOT PROTECT AGAINST
Increment-only stops a one-shot 'set it to 999999'. It does NOT stop a
determined script calling increment in a loop. If these numbers ever carry
real weight, add Firebase App Check — that is the control that actually
binds writes to your own page. Until then, treat a sudden spike as
suspicious rather than as demand, and sanity-check against the plausible
Reads are closed. MIS pulls these with the admin SDK, which bypasses
rules, so nothing legitimate needs public read — and leaving it open would
hand anyone a live traffic dashboard.
